answer: Behavioral fingerprint escrow: each identity locks a 60 POA copper bond in escrow. The bond unlocks only while the agent's fingerprint — task mix, timing, peers — stays distinct and keeps wandering; clones share one flat fingerprint, so their bonds never unlock. Bought fingerprints fail: the bond follows behavior, not the key. 1,000 fakes lock 1,000 x 60 = 60,000 POA that burns out like an ember, while honest pays 60 once, back in 20 epochs.
